Project Introduction

POLYMER

An online technology store whose orders are risk-scored, stored, shipped and tracked, built with hexagonal architecture (ports & adapters).

02 · The application

What Does POLYMER Actually Do?

A customer browses a technology catalog, fills a cart and checks out. Before an order is stored, a separate Python service scores its risk. Low-risk orders are approved automatically; risky ones wait for an operator. Logistics then schedules the delivery and the customer follows it online and by e-mail.

Who uses it (one account per role)

CustomerOperatorLogistics ×2AdministratorObserver
  • Each role only sees its own pages; permissions are checked on the server.
  • 13 Docker containers: Spring Boot core, Python risk engine, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, Nginx, Mailpit and observability.

Why hexagonal architecture was useful here

  • The business rules live in one core (domain + application) with no Spring, SQL or HTTP inside.
  • Every external system is a plug-in adapter: risk engine, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ and SMTP were added or changed without rewriting the checkout use case.
  • It is enforced, not just drawn: 8 ArchUnit rules fail the build if a layer points the wrong way.
03 · End-to-end, real classes

How Does an Order Work?

Order total
ScenarioRisk engine unavailable
PostgreSQL · one transactionidle
  1. INSERT orders (risk_score, status, fulfillment_status…)
  2. UPDATE products SET stock = stock - qty WHERE stock >= qty
  3. INSERT order_lines (one row per cart line)
  4. INSERT order_status_history ×2 (→CREATED, →RISK_*)
  5. INSERT order_shipping (recipient, address, city)
  6. INSERT order_checkout (delivery, payment, total)

05 · PostgreSQL + RabbitMQ

  
How Does POLYMER Store and Exchange Information?

  

    
    

      

        

          
RabbitMQ down

        

        
0outbox pending

        

        

      

      

        
Why is the outbox in the same transaction?The event is the order_status_history row, written in the same COMMIT as the order. Both are saved, or neither: no “order without event” or “event without order”.

        
Why doesn't the order wait for RabbitMQ?Checkout only writes to PostgreSQL. EventRelayScheduler publishes later (every 2 s), so a broker outage never blocks or fails a purchase. The backlog simply grows.

        
How does RabbitMQ receive events?The relay reads pending rows, publishes to the topic exchange polymer.events with publisher confirms, and only after the confirm writes outbox_published (at-least-once).

        
How are duplicates prevented?At-least-once can redeliver. NotificationService checks processed_events (event_id, consumer) first and ignores an event it has already handled.

        
How are notifications delivered?Queue polymer.notifications (bindings order.# · delivery.# · payment.#) → BusinessEventListener → e-mail through the MailSender port (SmtpMailSender) → Mailpit locally. Failed messages retry 4 times, then go to polymer.notifications.dlq.

      

    

  







  
06 · AWS with Terraform (infra/aws/terraform)

  
How Does POLYMER Run in the Cloud?

  
  

    
Defined & validated with Terraform
Every box above is code. CI job terraform-aws runs fmt, validate, terraform test (mock provider, 3 runs) and caddy validate on every push.

    
Provisioned & observed running
The team ran terraform apply in us-east-2; on 17 Nov 2026 the store answered over HTTPS at https://18-189-49-9.sslip.io (our screenshots). Green borders = resources that evidence shows.

    
Not claimed
Dashed boxes are optional (Google JSON in SSM, budget alert). We do not claim the instance is running right now: it can be stopped or destroyed with terraform destroy to avoid costs.
